fact: SERVICOM Presidency, with the World Bank's ESF Unit, launched the Nigeria Electronic Grievance Management platform in Abuja to receive and manage complaints and feedback on World Bank-supported projects and government institutions.

SERVICOM's acting National Coordinator says its Ministerial and Parastatal SERVICOM Units across MDAs let complaints be received, escalated, tracked and resolved across all tiers of government through the platform.
SERVICOM Presidency's National Coordinator announced that its Citizens E-Feedback portal, built into the SERVICOM website for complaints and commendations about MDA services, is now operational.

Data Science Nigeria says the Edo Citizens' Feedback System, built on a DHIS2 tracker program, lets residents report service gaps in schools, clinics and roads and has handled over 12,000 real-time reports (Edo State).
Nigeria's Public Complaints Commission chief commissioner said on 24 October 2025 it is set to introduce an online portal for citizens to lodge complaints and track cases, with no launch date given.
ReportGov.ng, described as Nigeria's official public service complaint website, recorded complaints against agencies in November 2024, for example eight for FRSC and four for FAAN.
ReportGov.ng's monthly report covers complaints about many federal agencies, including NITDA, BPP, FRSC, NPA, FAAN and Customs.
ReportGov.ng's monthly report gives complaints received and resolved per agency for November 2024, for example FAAN four of four and NITDA none of two.
ReportGov.NG is described as Nigeria's official public service complaints and feedback website for the services of any federal MDA, with 53 MDAs ranked on engagement.
PEBEC's 2024 Half-Year Transparency and Efficiency Compliance Report ranked 53 MDAs, with NERC at 100 percent compliance with the 72-hour complaint resolution timeline.
